channel.title: Said & Checked: Courts and Nominations — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Courts and Nominations, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Courts and Nominations, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 2 unsettled (John Barrasso)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • John Barrasso, U.S. Senator from Wyoming: “For the first 227 years under our Constitution--1789 to 2016--this Senate confirmed 94 percent of judicial nominees by unanimous consent.” Unsupported. No published count of judicial nominees confirmed by unanimous consent from 1789 to 2016 was found. Searched: AskAmerica's judge and nomination tables (no vote-method data before 2017; nominations cover recent Congresses only) and one web search, which returned Supreme Court figures only. Senate historical records and academic studies were not searched further.
  • John Barrasso, U.S. Senator from Wyoming: “This Republican Senate has already confirmed judges at the fastest pace in decades.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's nominations data count 58 circuit, district and trade-court confirmations through Nov. 17, 2026, against 82 at the same point of Trump's first term (Nov. 18, 2018) and 83 of Biden's (Nov. 18, 2022). The rows behind these counts could not be read directly, and 'pace' could also mean speed per nomination, so the claim is not settled here.
  • John Barrasso, U.S. Senator from Wyoming: “Today, more judges who are serving in the Federal courts were nominated by President Trump compared to any other recent President.” Unsettled. In AskAmerica's Federal Judicial Center data, Trump appointees outnumber every other recent president's among active judges (279 against Obama's 211). Counting judges on senior status as serving, Obama leads 291 to 280. The statement does not say which reading it means.

10 statements by 2 officeholders. 6 checked: 3 supported, 2 unsettled, 1 unsupported · 4 not checkable.

item.title: Said & Checked, Courts and Nominations, 2026-11-17: none false or contradicted, 3 unsupported, 15 unsettled (John Thune, Dick Durbin)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported

  • John Thune, U.S. Senator from South Dakota (Senate Majority Leader): “we have confirmed 606 civilian nominees.” Unsupported. No count of civilian nominees confirmed in this Congress as of Nov. 16 was found; the nearest published figures are 301 confirmed en bloc as of May 2026 and 417 confirmations in 2025. The search covered web sources, a May 2026 Senate Republican leadership release and Senate vote pages; the majority leader's nominations tracker was not read.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “we heard from two nominees who have been out of law school for just 8 years. One of them has practiced law for just 7 years; the other has only practiced for 5 years.” Unsupported. No source giving the nominees' law school graduation or years of practice was found. The search covered the committee's Nov. 10 hearing page and two of the five nominees' questionnaires, which are scanned images with no readable text, plus a web search; the other three questionnaires and press coverage were not read.
  • Dick Durbin, U.S. Senator from Illinois: “That is less experience than any Biden nominee or any prior Trump nominee.” Unsupported. No comparison of these nominees' experience against all Biden and earlier Trump judicial nominees was found; the speaker's own Nov. 10 statement compares them with nominees heard by the committee in the last 10 years. The search covered the Congressional Record, the committee's Nov. 10 press release and coverage of that hearing; ABA ratings data and the Federal Judicial Center's biographical records were not searched.

29 statements by 2 officeholders. 26 checked: 8 supported, 15 unsettled, 3 unsupported · 3 not checkable.
